record.title: The topological representation theorem for tropical oriented matroids
record.statement: A tropical pseudohyperplane is a subset of $\mathbb{TP}^{d-1}$ that is PL-homeomorphic to a tropical hyperplane, and an arrangement is a collection of such tropical pseudohyperplanes. **Topological representation theorem.** Every tropical oriented matroid can be realized by an arrangement of tropical pseudohyperplanes. The theorem is presented as a consequence of the subdivision correspondence conjecture and would provide a topological representation analogous to representation theorems for ordinary oriented matroids.
record.source_name: Federico Ardila and Mike Develin, “Tropical hyperplane arrangements and oriented matroids”, arXiv:0706.2920 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.2920

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2007).

record.title: Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture for graphs of non-degenerate classical transportation polytopes
record.statement: Let $P_c=\{x\mid Bx=c,\ x\geq 0\}$ be a non-degenerate $m\times n$ classical transportation polytope, and let its graph have the vertices and edges of $P_c$. **Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture.** The graph of every non-degenerate $m\times n$ transportation polytope has a Hamiltonian cycle when $mn>4$. This conjecture arises from enumeration data on transportation polytopes; the supplied source does not state a resolution, so its general status is open.
record.source_name: Jesús A. De Loera, Edward D. Kim, Shmuel Onn and Francisco Santos, “Graphs of Transportation Polytopes”, arXiv:0709.2189 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.2189

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).

record.title: The logarithmic density bound for progression-free subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_4^n$
record.statement:
Let $G=\mathbb{Z}_4^n$, and let $A\subset G$ contain no proper three-term arithmetic progressions.

**Logarithmic density conjecture.** One should have

$$
|A|=O\left(\frac{|G|}{\log^{3/2}|G|}\right).
$$

This is a stronger analogue in $\mathbb{Z}_4^n$ of the Erdős–Turán conjecture. The preceding discussion explains that the methods of the paper would need a substantial improvement to reach this bound, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Tom Sanders, “Roth's theorem in Z_4^n”, arXiv:0807.5101 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.5101

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2008).

record.title: The relaxed Double-Critical Graph Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected double-critical $k$-chromatic graph. A graph is **contractible to** $K_k$ when it can be reduced to the complete $k$-graph by graph contractions.

**Relaxed Double-Critical Graph Conjecture.** Every double-critical $k$-chromatic graph is contractible to the complete $k$-graph.

This is posed as a weaker version of Hadwiger's Conjecture. The source gives no resolution status for this relaxed conjecture, so it remains open.
record.source_name: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Anders Sune Pedersen and Bjarne Toft, “Double-critical graphs and complete minors”, arXiv:0810.3133 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.3133

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2008). “Hadwiger's Conjecture is one of the most fundamental conjectures of Graph Theory, much effort has gone into settling it, but it remains open for $k \geq 7$.”

record.title: The well-quasi-ordering conjecture for finite-field-representable matroids
record.statement:
Let $\mathrm{GF}(q)$ be a finite field. A set of matroids is **well-quasi-ordered** by the minor relation when every infinite set contains two matroids, one of which is isomorphic to a minor of the other.

**Well-quasi-ordering conjecture.** Any infinite set of $\mathrm{GF}(q)$-representable matroids contains two matroids, one of which is isomorphic to a minor of the other.

A positive answer would imply that every minor-closed class of $\mathrm{GF}(q)$-representable matroids has finitely many $\mathrm{GF}(q)$-representable excluded minors. The conjecture is attributed to Neil Robertson and Paul Seymour and is discussed in the context of extending the Graph Minors project to matroids representable over finite fields; its resolution is not supplied here.
record.source_name: Dillon Mayhew, Gordon Royle and Geoff Whittle, “Excluding Kuratowski graphs and their duals from binary matroids”, arXiv:0902.0198 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.0198

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2009).

record.title: The dual colorful Tverberg theorem in the plane
record.statement: Let $3n$ straight lines in general position be given in the plane, and partition them into three color classes of $n$ lines each. **The dual colorful Tverberg theorem.** The lines can be partitioned into $n$ colorful triples, each containing one line of every color, such that the triangles formed by the triples have a common point. This is proposed as a dual analogue of the colorful Tverberg theorem in the plane; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or remains open.
record.source_name: R. N. Karasev, “Dual central point theorems and their generalizations”, arXiv:0909.4915 (2009).

record.title: Greedy bubble factorization conjecture for permutation matrices
record.statement: Let $P$ be a finite permutation matrix of bandwidth $w>0$. A **greedy bubble matrix** of $P$ is a product of reducing and overtaking swaps of $P$ such that $P$ and the resulting matrix $GP$ have no common inverted pairs. **Greedy bubble factorization conjecture.** $P$ is the product of fewer than $2w$ greedy bubble matrices. The conjecture proposes a bound on the number of greedy bubble steps needed to factor a permutation matrix, building on computations for permutation matrices of order at most $9$; the supplied source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Michael Daniel Samson and Martianus Frederic Ezerman, “Factoring Permutation Matrices Into a Product of Tridiagonal Matrices”, arXiv:1007.3467 (2010).

record.title: The $(k-1,1)$ minor conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $G$ be a $k$-chromatic graph. A **minor** is obtained by vertex deletions, edge deletions and edge contractions; $K_{a,b}$ denotes the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $a$ and $b$.

**$(k-1,1)$ minor conjecture.** Every $k$-chromatic graph has either a $K_k$ minor or a

$$
K_{\left\lfloor \frac{k+1}{2} \right\rfloor,\left\lceil \frac{k+1}{2} \right\rceil}
$$

minor.

The conjecture is presented as a well-known relaxed version of Hadwiger's conjecture; no resolution is supplied in the paper excerpt.
record.source_name: Anders Sune Pedersen, “Complete and almost complete minors in double-critical 8-chromatic graphs”, arXiv:1007.5400 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.5400

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2010). “The case $k=5$ of Hadwiger's Conjecture was finally settled in the affirmative with Appel and Haken's proof of the Four Colour Theorem (an improved proof was subsequently published in 1997 by Robertson et al. ).”

record.title: Laman-spanning conjecture for the $(3+2)$-core of a random graph
record.statement: Let $G(n,c/n)$ be an Erdős–Rényi random graph, and let $c_2$ be the threshold above which the $(3+2)$-core emerges. A subgraph is **Laman-spanning** if it contains a spanning Laman graph. **Laman-spanning conjecture.** With high probability, the entire $(3+2)$-core is Laman-spanning in $G(n,c/n)$ for $c>c_2$. The conjecture concerns the structure of the rigid component beyond its emergence threshold; the source gives no resolution of this claim.
record.source_name: Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan, Cristopher Moore and Louis Theran, “The rigidity transition in random graphs”, arXiv:1010.3605 (2010).

record.title: Chan–Jensen–Rubei's tropical basis conjecture for matrix minors
record.statement: Let $d$, $n$, and $r$ be integers, and consider the $(r+1)\times(r+1)$ minors of a $d$-by-$n$ matrix. A collection of tropical polynomials is a **tropical basis** when its tropical zero set equals the tropicalization of the variety it defines. **Chan–Jensen–Rubei's conjecture.** The $(r+1)\times(r+1)$ minors of a $d$-by-$n$ matrix are a tropical basis if and only if either $r\leqslant2$ or $r\geqslant\min\{d,n\}-2$. This conjecture gives a proposed complete characterization of when determinantal minors form a tropical basis; the surrounding discussion relates it equivalently to equality of tropical and Kapranov rank bounds for matrices. Its resolution is not given in the source.
record.source_name: Yaroslav Shitov, “Example of a 6-by-6 Matrix with Different Tropical and Kapranov Ranks”, arXiv:1012.5507 (2010).

record.title: McDiarmid–Reed conjecture for triangle-free induced subgraphs of the triangular lattice
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free induced subgraph of the triangular lattice, and let $b$ be a positive integer. The graph $G$ is **$(a,b)$-colorable** if, when every vertex receives the same list of $a$ colors, one can choose $b$ colors at each vertex so that adjacent vertices receive disjoint color sets.

**McDiarmid–Reed conjecture.** Every triangle-free induced subgraph of the triangular lattice is

$$
\left(\left\lceil\frac{9b}{4}\right\rceil,b\right)\text{-colorable}.
$$

This conjecture concerns multicoloring for radio-frequency assignment on triangular-lattice networks. The source gives no resolution status; the paper proves the related list-coloring bound $(5m,2m)$ for finite triangle-free induced subgraphs, rather than the stated ordinary-coloring conjecture.
record.source_name: Yves Aubry, Jean-Christophe Godin and Olivier Togni, “Every triangle-free induced subgraph of the triangular lattice is (5m,2m)-choosable”, arXiv:1110.2650 (2011).
record.references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2011).

record.title: Class II characterization for regular graphs under adjacent vertex distinguishing total coloring by sum
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a $k$-regular graph. The graph is called $tndi_{\sum}$ class II when its adjacent vertex distinguishing index by sum attains the class-II value. **Class II characterization conjecture.** A $k$-regular graph $\Gamma$ is $tndi_{\sum}$ class II if and only if $\Gamma$ has a proper vertex $k+2$ coloring. The conjecture relates the class-II condition for regular graphs to ordinary proper vertex colorability with $k+2$ colors.
record.source_name: Hana Choi, Dongseok Kim, Sungjin Lee and Yeonhee Lee, “A proper total coloring distinguishing adjacent vertices by sums of some product graphs”, arXiv:1402.0615 (2014).

record.title: Erdős–Szemerédi sum-product conjecture
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{C}$. For $g\in\mathbb{N}$, define

$$
gA=\{a_1+\dots+a_g:a_1,\dots,a_g\in A\},\qquad A^{(g)}=\{a_1\dots a_g:a_1,\dots,a_g\in A\}.
$$

**Erdős–Szemerédi conjecture.** For any $g\in\mathbb{N}$, any $\varepsilon>0$ and any set $A\subseteq\mathbb{C}$, one should have

$$
\max\{\lvert gA\rvert,\lvert A^{(g)}\rvert\}\gg_{g,\varepsilon}\lvert A\rvert^{g-\varepsilon}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that additive and multiplicative structure cannot coexist too strongly. It generalizes the assertion that either the sumset or product set of a finite complex set must be close in size to $\lvert A\rvert^2$; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

record.title: Erdős–Sós conjecture for trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $t$ vertices. For a graph $G$, write $e(G)$ for its number of edges, and call $G$ **$T$-free** if it contains no subgraph isomorphic to $T$. **Erdős–Sós conjecture.** If $T$ is a tree on $t$ vertices, then every $T$-free graph $G$ on $N$ vertices satisfies

$$
e(G)\leq \frac{t-2}{2}N.
$$

This is the classical linear extremal conjecture for trees, introduced by Erdős. The paper studies its restriction to bipartite host graphs; the general conjecture is presented here without a supplied resolution status.

record.title: K4-minor conjecture for negative coefficients of graph independence Rayleigh differences
record.statement: Let $\mathsf G$ be a graph and let $e,f$ be edges of $\mathsf G$. Write $\Delta Z(\mathbf I\mathsf G)\{e,f\}$ for the Rayleigh difference of the independence-set partition function. **K4-minor conjecture.** If this polynomial has a negative coefficient, then $\mathsf G$ has a $\mathsf K_4$-minor in which the images of $e$ and $f$ occur on nonadjacent edges. The conjecture implies the adjacent-edge coefficient conjecture and remains open in the source.
record.source_name: David G. Wagner, “Negatively correlated random variables and Mason's conjecture”, arXiv:math/0602648 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0602648

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2006). “A positive solution to the Big Conjecture would be a very good thing.”

record.title: Minor-closedness conjecture for maximal cut-ideal generating degree
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $I_G$ be its cut ideal, and let $\mu(I_G)$ denote the maximal degree of a binomial in a minimal generating set of $I_G$. A graph $H$ is a **minor** of $G$ if it is obtained from $G$ by deleting and contracting edges. **Minor-closedness conjecture.** For any $k$, the set of graphs $G$ such that

$$
\mu(I_G) \leq k
$$

is minor-closed. This would characterize graphs with bounded cut-ideal generating degree by finitely many excluded minors, in view of the Robertson–Seymour graph-minor theorem. The conjecture is supported by the fact that induced-subgraph formation and edge contraction correspond to faces of cut polytopes, and hence cannot increase generating degrees; deletion of edges is the remaining case, and its effect is not established here.
record.source_name: Bernd Sturmfels and Seth Sullivant, “Toric geometry of cuts and splits”, arXiv:math/0606683 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0606683

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2006).

record.title: Quartic generation conjecture for cut ideals
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $I_G$ be its cut ideal. A graph is **$K_5$-minor-free** when it has no minor isomorphic to $K_5$. **Quartic generation conjecture.**

$$
I_G \text{ is generated in degrees }\leq 4\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G \text{ is }K_5\text{-minor-free}.
$$

This extends the proposed characterization for quadratic generation. It is presented as a conjectural description of the complexity of Markov bases for graph cuts, and the authors also suggest that it captures the class of graphs with normal and Cohen–Macaulay cut ideals; that latter relationship is stated separately below.

record.title: Thomassen's conjecture for nonorientable surface triangulations
record.statement:
Let a triangulation of a nonorientable surface have Euler genus $g$, and let $h$ be an integer satisfying

$$
1 \leq h < g.
$$

Let an **NSC** be a noncontractible separating cycle; the two surfaces separated by it are understood after capping the boundary components with disks.

**Nonorientable analogue of Thomassen's conjecture.** Every such triangulation contains an NSC such that the two surfaces separated by the NSC have Euler genera $h$ and $g-h$, respectively.

This conjecture prescribes the Euler genera of the two pieces, strengthening the assertion that an NSC exists. The surrounding text presents it as an analogue of Thomassen's orientable-surface conjecture; no general resolution is given.
record.source_name: Thom Sulanke, “Irreducible triangulations of low genus surfaces”, arXiv:math/0606690 (2006).

record.title: Polynomial-time recognition conjecture for APUD(1,1)
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mathrm{APUD}(1,1)$ denote the corresponding graph class of restricted disk intersection graphs.

**APUD(1,1) recognition conjecture.** Given a graph $G$, it can be determined whether $G\in\mathrm{APUD}(1,1)$ in polynomial time.

The preceding characterization gives necessary structural conditions for connected graphs in $\mathrm{APUD}(1,1)$, but the source does not establish that they are sufficient. Polynomial-time recognition therefore remains an open problem.

record.title: Polynomial-time minor containment conjecture for fixed codes
record.statement:
Fix a code ${\mathcal M}$. Given a code ${\mathcal C}$ of length $n$, **polynomial-time minor-containment conjecture.** It is decidable in time polynomial in $n$ whether ${\mathcal C}$ contains ${\mathcal M}$ as a minor.

This is an algorithmic counterpart to finite excluded-minor characterizations: testing containment of a fixed minor would provide an efficient recognition procedure for the corresponding excluded-minor class. The source gives no resolution status.
